title: What If Every Wasp on Earth Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every wasp vanished? Most people would cheer. Scientists would not.
There are roughly 33,000 species of stinging wasps, and few are the picnic crashers you picture.
Many are hunters, going after aphids and caterpillars, the pests that eat crops.
Insect pest control is worth at least 416 billion dollars a year, and wasps are mostly missing from that math.
Wasps also visit 960 plant species for pollination, and 164 of those plants depend on wasps completely.
Some orchids even mimic a female wasp. Scientists say wasps could be as valuable as bees, if we gave them a chance.
